hyperedges.label: OpenSpec change lifecycle (propose, apply, update, sync, archive)

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging principle
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: Spec sync is agent-driven rather than programmatic because a delta expresses intent, not a wholesale replacement: partial updates (adding one scenario without copying existing ones) need judgement that a mechanical merge cannot provide.

nodes.label: Header Responsive Mobile Change Proposal
nodes.rationale: The five-element single-row header exceeds 375px on phones; the fix is Tailwind-only changes across five header component files with no game logic changes, building on the previous responsive pass.

nodes.label: Header Gap Responsive Spacing Requirement (delta into responsive-layout)
nodes.norm_label: header gap responsive spacing requirement (delta into responsive-layout)

nodes.label: Responsive Adaptation Change Proposal
nodes.rationale: The app was desktop-only with a fixed 3-panel layout, breaking on phones and tablets; the goal is playability below 1024px via CSS-class-only changes across 13 component files with no logic changes.

nodes.label: Header Container Gap Reduction on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: header container gap reduction on mobile
nodes.rationale: A 32px gap between stats and actions is wasteful on mobile; 12px keeps visual separation while fitting more content in a 375px viewport.

nodes.label: Hide Entire HeaderTitle Block on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: hide entire headertitle block on mobile
nodes.rationale: The title (icon plus text, ~200px) is decorative; players already know the game they are playing. Removing both icon and text frees space for functional elements, and keeping only the icon was rejected as not worth its footprint.

nodes.label: Pause Button min-width Removal on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: pause button min-width removal on mobile
nodes.rationale: The pause button text is already hidden on mobile, leaving an icon-only button (~32px); min-w-[84px] was forcing 84px of empty width, so the button should shrink to natural content width. A separate icon-only button variant was rejected as overkill.

nodes.label: Settings Button Shrinks From 40px to 32px on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: settings button shrinks from 40px to 32px on mobile
nodes.rationale: 40px is oversized for a secondary action on mobile; 32px saves space while keeping a usable tap target. Known risk: 32px is below Apple's 44px HIG guideline, mitigated because settings is low-frequency during gameplay.

nodes.label: Stat Value Font Reduction on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: stat value font reduction on mobile
nodes.rationale: Smaller text (text-xs) lets stat pills narrow while remaining readable, since money and baked-count values are short numeric strings.

nodes.label: Conditional Visibility via hidden/block Utilities
nodes.rationale: The Date stat and pause button text are redundant on small screens; hiding them with Tailwind hidden/lg:block reclaims space without losing functionality, while the icon-only pause button stays usable.

nodes.label: Flexible Modal Heights (h-auto max-h-80vh)
nodes.rationale: Fixed heights like h-[600px] cause overflow or wasted space on small screens; h-auto adapts to content while max-h-[80vh] keeps the modal inside the viewport.

nodes.label: IndustryMap Horizontal Scroll Container on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: industrymap horizontal scroll container on mobile
nodes.rationale: The 5-stage map uses fixed w-32 stages; wrapping it in overflow-x-auto is the minimal change that preserves the desktop layout instead of restructuring the component. Risk: horizontal scroll may be undiscoverable, mitigated by visible stage cues.

nodes.label: lg (1024px) Breakpoint Strategy
nodes.rationale: The 3-panel layout needs ~1024px to display comfortably: below lg the layout stacks vertically, at or above lg the desktop layout stays unchanged. The md (768px) breakpoint was judged too narrow for the 3-panel layout and a custom breakpoint unnecessary complexity.

nodes.label: Vertical Stacking of GameScreen Panels on Mobile
nodes.norm_label: vertical stacking of gamescreen panels on mobile
nodes.rationale: flex-col on mobile with flex-row on desktop is the simplest approach requiring no JavaScript; vertical scrolling is natural on touch devices. Tabs and drawers were rejected as over-engineered.

nodes.label: Explore Mode is a Stance, Not a Workflow
nodes.norm_label: explore mode is a stance, not a workflow
nodes.rationale: Thinking time must stay open-ended and unscripted: the agent may read/search the codebase and even create OpenSpec artifacts (capturing thinking) but must never write application code inside explore mode.

nodes.label: Fluid Workflow Integration (actions on a change)
nodes.norm_label: fluid workflow integration (actions on a change)
nodes.rationale: Implementation is not phase-locked: apply can run anytime (before all artifacts are done, interleaved with other actions) and may reveal design issues that should flow back into artifact updates instead of blocking.

nodes.label: Update vs. Start Fresh heuristic
nodes.rationale: If a request changes the change's intent rather than refining it, revising artifacts would distort the plan, so a fresh change (/opsx-new) is recommended instead.

nodes.label: Zustand gameStore Single Serializable Store
nodes.rationale: All game state lives in one Zustand store (gameStore.ts) as serializable data plus action functions; only the serializable fields need persistence, since actions are defined in code.

nodes.label: Continue Last Session Flow
nodes.rationale: Continue resumes a valid save and skips GameSettingsScreen; corrupted or missing saves fall back to the new-game path without mutating current state, so the welcome screen only shows the button when a valid envelope exists.

nodes.label: Save Game Change Proposal (save-only localStorage persistence)
nodes.norm_label: save game change proposal (save-only localstorage persistence)
nodes.rationale: Players lose all progress on refresh because game state is ephemeral; auto-save to localStorage enables session continuity with zero user effort. Scope is deliberately save-only, with load/restore deferred to a separate specification and no breaking changes.

nodes.label: Always-Active Auto-Save Mount in App.tsx
nodes.rationale: Calling useAutoSave() unconditionally in App.tsx saves default state even before play begins, so there is always something to restore once load is implemented, and avoids conditional mount logic.

nodes.label: Custom useAutoSave Hook Instead of Zustand Persist Middleware
nodes.norm_label: custom useautosave hook instead of zustand persist middleware
nodes.rationale: zustand/middleware/persist serializes the entire store including ~15 non-serializable action functions, makes the save format opaque, and offers no beforeunload safety net; a custom hook gives explicit field selection, a versioned envelope, and unload handling. Persistent Zustand middleware was explicitly rejected.

nodes.label: Explicit Pick of Saveable GameState Fields
nodes.norm_label: explicit pick of saveable gamestate fields
nodes.rationale: An explicit Pick of every saveable field is self-documenting and type-safe, and fails at compile time if a store field is added without updating the save type, unlike runtime JSON.stringify plus filtering.

nodes.label: 5-Second Save Interval Aligned With Game Tick
nodes.norm_label: 5-second save interval aligned with game tick
nodes.rationale: SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 5000 matches DAY_DURATION_MS so every save reflects a meaningful tick state change with no redundant writes; the beforeunload handler covers the gap between intervals.

nodes.label: Versioned SaveData Envelope Format
nodes.rationale: The version field enables future migration and load-time validation if the state shape changes; savedAt provides last-saved UI metadata and debugging aid at minimal overhead.

nodes.label: Centered Rounded Hero Card on Dark Brown Background
nodes.norm_label: centered rounded hero card on dark brown background

nodes.label: Emphasized Phrase 'every crumb counts' in Paragraph
nodes.norm_label: emphasized phrase 'every crumb counts' in paragraph

nodes.label: OpenSpec Spec-Driven Configuration
nodes.rationale: Project-level OpenSpec config declaring schema: spec-driven plus optional project context and per-artifact rules used when creating proposals, tasks, and specs.

nodes.label: index.html entry point with dark-mode bootstrap
nodes.norm_label: index.html entry point with dark-mode bootstrap

nodes.label: loadFromStorage() utility (src/utils/loadFromStorage.ts)
nodes.rationale: Loading is a one-shot action triggered by a click, not reactive state, so a plain function is simpler and more testable than a hook; failures return false so callers can fall back to the normal flow.

nodes.label: useHasSave hook (src/hooks/useHasSave.ts)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous single localStorage read + JSON parse on mount is cheap and used in one place, so a self-contained hook beats a context/provider; validating the parsed shape (not just key existence) keeps the Continue button hidden for corrupted saves.

nodes.label: WelcomeButton component (src/features/welcome/layout/WelcomeButton.tsx)
nodes.rationale: hasSave plus an onContinue callback lets one component render either the two-button layout or the original single Next button, keeping existing behaviour unchanged when no save exists.
